title: PostgreSQL MVCC Internals: Heap Tuples, xmin, xmax, and Hints
realWorldScenario: During an audit of the `loans` table, a junior engineer notices that after running an `UPDATE loans SET status = 'ACTIVE'` on 10,000 rows, the table size on disk doubled from 50MB to 100MB even though the row count remained identical.
questionStatement: Explain PostgreSQL Multi-Version Concurrency Control (MVCC) at the physical tuple level. What are `xmin`, `xmax`, `t_ctid`, and `infomask` hint bits in the heap tuple header? Describe step-by-step how an UPDATE statement is executed physically on disk.
expectedConcepts: t_ctid pointer chaining between tuple versions
Hint bits (HEAP_XMIN_COMMITTED) preventing repeat pg_xact lookups
Why UPDATE is physically an INSERT + soft-delete
hints: Remember that PostgreSQL never modifies an existing tuple in place during an UPDATE.
What fields in the 23-byte tuple header record transaction visibility?
How does PostgreSQL know whether a transaction committed without reading the commit log every time?
